markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the person announces their candidacy.
markets.rules_primary: If Chris Deluzio has announced that they will run for the Class 3 United States Senate seat from Pennsylvania in 2028 after Issuance and before Feb 16, 2028, including running for the nomination of any political party to contest that office, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market is not mutually exclusive and multiple markets may resolve to Yes.

The person must publicly announce their campaign for it to be reported by a Source Agency. Merely filing campaign paperwork with the Federal Election Commission or similar entity is insufficient without a public announcement. Running for a party's nomination to contest the office counts as running for that office. The announcement must come from the person themselves or their official campaign, not from speculation or third-party sources.

An announcement made before Issuance does NOT resolve Yes. Announcing a campaign to contest this seat as an independent, or for any party's nomination, resolves YES. A person who announces and later withdraws still resolves YES.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If a bill capping federal student loan interest rates has passed the House after Issuance and before Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying bill is legislation that would set, for at least one category of federal student loan, a maximum interest rate lower than the maximum applicable to that category under the law in force on the Issuance date. A rate of zero qualifies. Legislation that re-enacts or technically amends the existing maximums without lowering any of them does NOT qualify, and neither does a cap on fees, monthly payments or total repayment.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules, a special rule or a discharge petition. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains a qualifying cap. Committee approval, a rule providing for consideration, or a discharge petition reaching 218 signatures without passage does NOT count. Senate passage, enactment, and a cap imposed by regulation rather than by the House do NOT count.
markets.title: Will a bill capping federal student loan interest rates passed the House before Jan 3, 2027?

markets.rules_primary: If a New York State court grants the petitioners preliminary or permanent injunctive or annulment relief (other than a temporary restraining order) against the City's supplemental tax roll, its surcharge notices, or its imposition or collection of the pied-à-terre surcharge in O'Brien v. City of New York, or any appeal thereof before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market resolves on a written court ruling in O'Brien v. City of New York, the Article 78 proceeding brought in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, Richmond County by Rachel O'Brien, Carmine Morano and Simon Hedley against Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Finance Commissioner Richard Lee over the rollout of the non-primary residence (pied-à-terre) surcharge. Rulings in any appeal of that proceeding also count.

The ruling must:

Be issued by a New York State court in O'Brien v. City of New York, or any appeal thereof
Address the specific matter described in the judgment
Be issued through a written order, opinion, judgment, or decision

Relief on any one of the three heads is enough, and partial relief counts. An order that annuls or enjoins the supplemental tax roll, the surcharge notices, or the imposition or collection of the surcharge resolves this market to YES.

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:

Oral rulings from the bench unless reduced to a written order
Tentative rulings that are not made final
Draft opinions that leak but are not officially issued
Settlements or voluntary dismissals
Administrative or scheduling orders
Orders to show cause
Minute orders that do not address the substantive issue in the judgment

The following also do NOT count, because they grant no injunctive or annulment relief:

The temporary restraining order issued August 10, 2026, or any later temporary restraining order
An order granting, confirming, vacating or dissolving a stay
Denial of a motion to dismiss or of any other dispositive motion
Voluntary action by the City, such as withdrawing notices, removing the tax roll, or extending a deadline

For clarity:

If the case is dismissed for lack of jurisdiction, that counts as a ruling only if the judgment refers to jurisdiction
Sua sponte rulings count if they match the judgment
Per curiam opinions and summary orders count as rulings
If multiple judges issue separate opinions, the majority/plurality opinion controls
A ruling in a separate proceeding that has not been consolidated into this one does not count
If no qualifying ruling is issued after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, this market resolves to NO
markets.title: Will a New York State court rule grants the petitioners preliminary or permanent injunctive or annulment relief (other than a temporary restraining order) against the City's supplemental tax roll, its surcharge notices, or its imposition or collection of the pied-à-terre surcharge?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the government is officially formed.
markets.rules_primary: If a coalition that includes Swedish Social Democratic Party make up the next elected ruling government of Sweden before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market is not mutually exclusive and multiple markets may resolve to Yes.

A party is considered to be part of government if one or more of its representatives hold at least one ministerial or cabinet-level position (including junior ministers or equivalent executive roles, if applicable) in the new government. This evaluation shall occur at the first official, stable formation of the government (i.e., once the legislative process for forming a government is complete and the head of state appoints ministers under normal non-caretaker circumstances).
A party whose representatives hold at least one ministerial or cabinet-level position — in Sweden, office as a minister (statsråd) — resolves YES
A party that only supports the government from outside it, under a confidence and supply or cooperation agreement of the kind the Sweden Democrats held under the 2022 Tidö Agreement, and holds no ministerial or cabinet-level position, does NOT resolve Yes
Political appointees in the Government Offices who are not ministers — state secretaries (statssekreterare), political advisers and coordination-office staff — are NOT ministerial or cabinet-level positions
Holding seats in the Riksdag is neither required nor sufficient. Swedish ministers do not have to be members of the Riksdag

The government evaluated is the first government formed following the Swedish general election of September 13, 2026. The transitional government that remains in office until that government is appointed is a caretaker government and does not count. markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary:
If the June 2027 BLS Employment Cost Index value used under Connecticut General Statutes §31-58 produces a Connecticut minimum fair wage for January 1, 2028 that is above 

$18.00 per hour, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Under Connecticut law, the January 1, 2028 rate is determined by the 12-month percentage change in the applicable ECI through June 30, 2027, with the resulting wage rounded to the nearest cent.

Resolution uses the 12-month percent change ending June 2027, not seasonally adjusted, for wages and salaries for all civilian workers. The January 1, 2028 minimum wage is calculated by applying that percentage change to the January 1, 2027 Connecticut minimum wage of $17.48 and rounding the resulting hourly wage to the nearest cent, consistent with Connecticut General Statutes §31-58. The market does not rely on the timing or wording of a subsequent Connecticut government announcement.

Resolution source: United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics - Employment Cost Index, Table 8: Employment Cost Index for wages and salaries, for civilian workers, by occupational group and industry, not seasonally adjusted.
markets.title: Will Connecticut minimum fair wage for January 1, 2028 be above $18.00 per hour?
